description: MMS gate: run the inline esm-spec 6.6 tests of problems/advection_1d_ppm_periodic.esm (model AdvectionPPM, test mms_transport) at the problem's default resolution (N=64) through each binding's official simulation pathway. Pins the PPM lowering (ic wiring at t=0), the transport error bound at t=0.1, and EXACT conservation (mean(u) preserved to the bit). The assertions and their tolerances live in the problem file itself; this manifest only routes the runners.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Rust TERMINATES at this manifest's own tolerance (Erk 1e-10/1e-12, ~6 s) as of EarthSciAST dc76c5bf: the whole-array overlay retired the hang, so the previous note's premise ('terminates only at reltol >= 1e-6') is obsolete. The gate it still misses is the one that note named: mms_transport[2] L2_error 2.155427189603012e-3 (rust) vs 2.1554288683622116e-3 (julia), 7.8e-7 relative -- outside the 1e-9 cross-binding-actuals floor. NOTE the convergence case of the same name IS armed for Rust: it gates against the committed golden/errors.json, which Rust matches at every resolution. Reproduced bit-identically across two independent runs, so this is a deterministic Erk-vs-Tsit5 method-disagreement floor, not flakiness and not a discretization error. MEASURED 2026-07-28 against EarthSciAST dc76c5bf via scripts/runners/run-rust.sh. Re-arm when both bindings run the same integrator, or when SIM_CROSS_RTOL in scripts/compare-outputs.py admits solver-method disagreement -- the sibling cases advection_2d_x_zero_grad_central and advection_2d_y_zero_grad_central are excluded for exactly this reason and nothing else.
